text_excerpts.doc_title: TITAN Earnings call transcript, filed 11-Aug-2026 (about Q1_FY2027, filing date, confirmed by the document)
text_excerpts.excerpt: The second bit was buyer growth of 5% when gold prices are stable.

text_excerpts.doc_title: TITAN Earnings call transcript, filed 11-Aug-2026 (about Q1_FY2027, filing date, confirmed by the document)
text_excerpts.excerpt: The second question was on the margin bit again that if you look at it organically, there has been a slight moderation in the margin, and we've obviously seen more than a 30% kind of an LFL growth this quarter.

text_excerpts.doc_title: TITAN Earnings call transcript, filed 11-Aug-2026 (about Q1_FY2027, filing date, confirmed by the document)
text_excerpts.excerpt: So when we say the 11% EBIT margin, what will be the driver sort of for this to improve?
text_excerpts.period_basis: filing date, confirmed by the document

text_excerpts.doc_title: TITAN Earnings call transcript, filed 11-Aug-2026 (about Q1_FY2027, filing date, confirmed by the document)
text_excerpts.excerpt: I think it is too early to just see June month, whether it was more than 5% and -- but I think that granular level of month-by-month growth, I don't think we want to.
text_excerpts.period_basis: filing date, confirmed by the document

text_excerpts.doc_title: TITAN Earnings call transcript, filed 11-Aug-2026 (about Q1_FY2027, filing date, confirmed by the document)
text_excerpts.excerpt: So in a scenario where gold price inflation is zero, do you think we can sort of maintain a 18% to 20% kind of top line growth in that kind of a scenario?
text_excerpts.period_basis: filing date, confirmed by the document

text_excerpts.doc_title: TITAN Earnings call transcript, filed 11-Aug-2026 (about Q1_FY2027, filing date, confirmed by the document)
text_excerpts.excerpt: And I'm not talking only about Q4, although the anniversarization happens in Q4, this is more of a general or a structural kind of a query that if for a few quarters, the Y-o-Y gold price inflation is zero in that scenario, does our growth rate come down versus our targeted 18% to 20% band?
text_excerpts.period_basis: filing date, confirmed by the document

text_excerpts.doc_title: TITAN Earnings call transcript, filed 11-Aug-2026 (about Q1_FY2027, filing date, confirmed by the document)
text_excerpts.excerpt: And in context of that, do you expect sort of the headwind on your margins to sort of maybe turn into a tailwind and you could see even with a slightly lower growth being able to deliver that 18% to 20% bottom line growth?
text_excerpts.period_basis: filing date, confirmed by the document

text_excerpts.doc_title: TITAN Earnings call transcript, filed 11-Aug-2026 (about Q1_FY2027, filing date, confirmed by the document)
text_excerpts.excerpt: Overall, long term, growth is on a very strong wicket, but the normalized margin would be gradually gravitating towards 12% to 15%, 16%.
text_excerpts.period_basis: filing date, confirmed by the document

text_excerpts.doc_title: TITAN Earnings call transcript, filed 11-Aug-2026 (about Q1_FY2027, filing date, confirmed by the document)
text_excerpts.excerpt: And in the long term, even depending on how the jewellery industry gold price dynamics work out, they can either progress towards 11% or stay around that number.
